title: How AI UI Generators Ingest Design Systems: Lovable vs v0 vs Figma Make vs Replit
content:
# How AI UI Generators Ingest Design Systems: A Comparison

Synthesis across the four tools' primary documentation, current as of August 2026. All four now have a real design system story — as recently as early 2025 only v0 did.

## The mechanisms differ architecturally

| Tool | Ingestion | Storage unit | Token source | Distribution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Lovable** | Design system *is* a Lovable project; local source or npm wrapper | .lovable/ (design-system.json, system.md, rules/*.md) | src/index.css custom properties or tailwind.config, auto-discovered | **File copy** into src/design-system/<slug>/, recorded in lovable.toml |
| **v0** | GitHub repos (max 3) + Figma nodes + docs links + npm/.tgz | Design system as a **skill**, configured by v0.json | Inferred from package + consumer app; legacy path via tokens.css / Tailwind config | Referenced skill, attachable per-chat; team default |
| **Figma Make** | npm package (public or Figma-hosted private registry) + published Figma library variables + guidelines | **Make kit**, published org-wide | **Both** code tokens and Figma library variables/styles | Published kit appears in teammates' kit selector |
| **Replit** | Component library **tarfile** upload + Figma import | custom_instruction/instructions.md (always-on) + .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (on-demand) | Design tokens file inside the skill; themes via shadcn CSS vars / TweakCN | **Pinned template app**, member access Read-only |

## The most important differentiator

**Figma Make is the only tool that reads tokens from the design source of truth.** Make kits ingest published Figma library variables and styles *alongside* the production npm package. Every other tool derives tokens from code only — Figma is a visual or screenshot input at best in v0 and Replit.

If a team's tokens live authoritatively in Figma variables, only Figma Make closes that loop without an export pipeline. Figma also claims the only prototype-to-production path: build in Make against the real package, then ship via the Figma MCP Server using the same components.

## The most important shared limitation

**All four are forward-only.** v0 states existing projects retain their original code and only new chats use updated design systems. Lovable requires accepting an update that overwrites local edits under src/design-system/. Replit distributes by pinned template, so existing apps don't inherit changes. Nobody solves design system version migration across already-generated apps.

## Gating is stratified

- Lovable design systems: **Enterprise-only**
- Replit design systems: **Enterprise-only** (Custom Instructions reach Pro)
- Figma Make kits: **Full seats on paid plans** plus **org admin approval** to publish
- v0 Design Systems 2.0: paid team plans for defaults, **Vercel Developer role** for private package env vars

No tool offers real design system import on a free or individual tier — prompt-level styling is the ceiling there.

## Everyone converged on React + Tailwind + shadcn, and it is a hard floor

Lovable supports "React-based component libraries out of the box" (Vue/Angular/Svelte require consultation). Make kits "exclusively support React-based codebases," pinned to React 18 and Vite. Replit and v0 are shadcn-derived.

Vercel states outright: "v0 is specifically trained on the default implementations of the shadcn/ui components and may struggle with any customizations" — the sharpest documented limitation in this space, and a trained-prior problem no config fixes.

Practitioners with non-React systems, React 19, or heavily customized shadcn forks should expect degraded results across the board.

## Nobody enforces at the component level

All four constrain generation through **prose guidelines plus available imports**. None can hard-fail a generation that hand-rolls a div instead of using your Button. Constraint is probabilistic everywhere.

## Two competing philosophies on context volume

Figma warns "more context isn't always better. It can confuse the LLM." Replit says "small, well-scoped skills combine cleanly. A skill that tries to cover everything tends to crowd out the skills that should have fired instead," and splits always-on instructions from on-demand skills. Lovable splits the auto-generated design-system.json/rules/ from the hand-authored, never-regenerated system.md.

The consistent lesson: a thin always-loaded layer plus progressively-disclosed detail beats one large knowledge dump.

## Auto-generation of agent-facing docs is becoming a category feature

Figma Make can "analyze your npm packages and library styles and write comprehensive guidelines for you." Lovable renders rules/components.md and rules/design-tokens.md from its schema. v0 reads the component surface from sources and builds a validating starter app.

Design system teams increasingly review AI-drafted agent documentation rather than authoring it — but every vendor still requires humans to supply the semantic layer (token hierarchy, quirks, constraints, when-not-to-use) that cannot be inferred from a type surface.
